sentences.text: Hintighernia is a newly described genus and species of tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cambridge Greensand of the United Kingdom.
The species is known from a partial cranium that had previously been assigned to the genus Ornithostoma.
The generic name combines the Brittonic words hɨnt (“lord”) and tɨɣern (“path”), meaning “Lord of the Paths”.
The specific epithet edingerae honors German paleontologist Johanna Ottilie Edinger, founder of paleoneurology.
Europe is interpreted as an early hotspot of tapejarid phylogenetic diversity and a possible origin point for sinopterines in Eastern Laurasia and tapejarines in South America.
The genus Hintighernia and its species edingerae were formally named by Pêgas et al. in 2026.
Micro-CT scanning shows that Hintighernia’s neuroanatomy closely resembles that of the tapejarid Tapejara wellnhoferi.
The partial cranium CAMSM B54406, previously referred to Ornithostoma sedgwicki, is identified as a sinopterine tapejarid and assigned to Hintighernia edingerae.
Additional Cambridge Greensand remains are referred to Tapejaridae, and an isolated rostral fragment is tentatively assigned to cf. Hintighernia.
The type species of the genus is Hintighernia edingerae.
Hintighernia lived during the Early Cretaceous.
Ornithostoma sedgwicki is considered a chaoyangopterid azhdarchoid known only from four jaw fragments.
Researchers suggest that a third, non-azhdarchid azhdarchoid species may also be present in the Cambridge Greensand.
